description: Maintained caption + attribution layer. Every record is captioned and attributed. Sources, in priority order: SGPHS timeline figcaptions (caption + credit), provenance embedded in original collection filenames, and descriptive captions written from filename text and the researched date. Attribution is 'Unknown' only when no holder or creator can be established. Re-applied every pipeline run by apply_editorial_captions.

attribution_confidence_levels.confirmed: explicit published credit line (e.g. SGPHS timeline figcaption)
attribution_confidence_levels.high: named collection/institution/newspaper recorded in the source filename
attribution_confidence_levels.medium: aggregator platform named (e.g. Calisphere) but contributing institution not yet resolved
attribution_confidence_levels.low: weak provenance hint (e.g. eBay listing) — holder not established
attribution_confidence_levels.unknown: no holder or creator identifiable from any available source

img_17d9fad337a3fded.caption: Council house (ceremonial big house), Morongo Reservation, c. 1890s.
img_17d9fad337a3fded.attribution: Huntington Library, William H. Weinland Photograph Collection (photCL 39 vol. 3 (20)); the catalog file is a low-resolution comp
img_17d9fad337a3fded.caption_source: Huntington Library Weinland Collection — exact print verified by direct image comparison (2026-07-20)
img_17d9fad337a3fded.basis: Exact print located at the Huntington Library: 'Council house.', photCL 39 vol. 3 (20), in the album 'Potrero Photographs' (1880-1900) compiled by Sarah Morris, one of the reservation's first schoolteachers. The old label '1800' is impossible — photography did not exist until 1839. In Cahuilla ethnography the ceremonial big house (kishumnawat) housed the sacred bundle, the net (hereditary clan leader) and the nukil mourning ceremony; 'council house' is the period settlers' term on the album mount.

img_c39e3df610ea24d9.caption: Pauline Weaver (c. 1797-1867), first settler of the San Gorgonio Pass — posthumous artist's sketch; no photograph of Weaver is known.
img_c39e3df610ea24d9.attribution: Artist unknown; no institutional provenance established (the circulating 'Sharlot Hall Museum' credit is unverified; cf. Arizona Historical Society portrait file #61659)
img_c39e3df610ea24d9.caption_source: Provenance research 2026-07-21 — Sharlot Hall Museum photo archive + collections catalog and Arizona Memory Project searched directly
img_c39e3df610ea24d9.basis: A crosshatched artist's sketch, not a photograph and not a portrait from life: no verified photograph or documented life portrait of Weaver exists. Most plausibly a 1920s memorial-era drawing — publicity around his 1929 reinterment at Prescott produced Weaver artwork, and the Arizona Historical Society institutionally dates its companion Weaver sketch (file #61659) c. 1920s. Weaver petitioned Mexican authorities in 1845 (with Isaac Williams) for possession of the abandoned Rancho San Gorgonio — no confirmed grant is documented, so avoid 'granted'. He conveyed the ranch to Dr. Isaac W. Smith and left by 1857; died Camp Verde, A.T., June 21, 1867.

img_650198dd9e4987ea.caption: Egan Avenue near the railroad crossing, Beaumont, 1907 — Burt Carter's livery stable and the Funk Realty Co. office.
img_650198dd9e4987ea.attribution: Beaumont Library District, via Calisphere (CBEA_011, ark:/13030/c8tb167d)
img_650198dd9e4987ea.caption_source: Calisphere Beaumont Library District collection (CBEA_011) + sign readings at high magnification (2026-07-20)
img_650198dd9e4987ea.basis: Same photograph as Calisphere CBEA_011; the album mount is typed 'BEAUMONT 1907'. The old label 'Stagecoach downtown Beaumont, 1860' was wrong twice over: no stagecoach appears (these are freight and livery rigs), and no town existed here in 1860 — George Egan laid out San Gorgonio (renamed Beaumont 1886-87) only in 1884. The realty office's photographed sign reads 'FUNK REALTY CO'; Calisphere's title 'J. Drew Frank Realty' is most likely a cataloger's misreading, corroborated by the 'FUNK REALTY CO. REAL ESTATE' sign beside the 1911 Beaumont Bank (CBEA_108), a building BLD itself titles the Funk Building.

img_6f833a14a7764e47.caption: The Southern Pacific depot (built 1887), looking east, c. 1905-1915.
img_6f833a14a7764e47.attribution: Beaumont Library District, via Calisphere (CBEA_134, ark:/13030/c85x2881)
img_6f833a14a7764e47.basis: Same photograph as Calisphere CBEA_134, 'Southern Pacific Depot in Beaumont, looking east.' Calisphere records this larger depot was built in 1887 but carries no date for the photo; c. 1905-1915 is an editorial estimate from the Edwardian crowd's dress, the long steel consist and the electric/telegraph poles. The old date '1875' is untenable — 1875-76 is when the SP line itself crossed the pass (the stop was then called 'Summit'); the town wasn't named Beaumont until 1886-87.

img_4e8d4526096e0dd7.caption: Fifth & Egan — the San Gorgonio Mercantile Co., the post office (far left) and a pool hall, 1890s.
img_4e8d4526096e0dd7.attribution: Beaumont Library District, via Calisphere (CBEA_146, ark:/13030/c8h70f56); rights: Copyrighted — Laura May Stewart Trust

img_4e8d4526096e0dd7.basis: Same photograph as Calisphere CBEA_146. The old caption made the post office the subject; per the Calisphere description the post office is the small building at far left on the southwest corner, and the dominant two-story false-front is the San Gorgonio Mercantile Company ('GENERAL MERCHANDISE' on its sign) — still wearing the town's pre-1887 name. Previously thought absent from Calisphere; found 2026-07-20.

img_c15c20a838d86c18.caption: Grain harvest on the Stewart Ranch — traditionally dated 1883, the year Stewart homesteaded.

Calisphere carries no date; '1883' is the homestead year, not a documented photo date — Holmes (1912) has Stewart raising grain from 1884, and an established harvest crew of this size implies the operation's later years. A handwritten note on the mount reads (partly legibly) 'Stewart's thrashers — RR track in back.'

img_b08de96dbf496fab.caption: The Beaumont Hotel, built 1887 — later the Hotel Edinburgh; burned August 1909.
img_b08de96dbf496fab.attribution: Beaumont Library District, via Calisphere (CBEA_009, ark:/13030/c81v5d9b); photograph by C. C. Pierce & Co., Los Angeles
img_b08de96dbf496fab.basis: Same photograph as Calisphere CBEA_009, which dates it circa 1895 and credits C. C. Pierce & Co. of Los Angeles. The old '1890' was a guess.

Priest - Herbert Loren “Pete” Priest (1862-1946), teacher, newspaper writer and later assistant postmaster of Beaumont - beside a young citrus tree, probably a sweet orange, on freshly worked, newly graded land; on the knoll behind him stands a long, low, single-story institutional building that remains unidentified.

V. R. Priest as “father of H. L. Priest, assistant postmaster”), superseding the earlier unverified howderfamily.com attribution.
